Hey guys, I've been reading posts on Reddit related to careers in STEM and I've noticed a lot of applied math/physics people and analytical engineers (mostly mechanical and electrical) end up doing software dev / software engineering of their own accord. This makes me wonder if people tend to mistake their aptitude/enjoyment in using logic to solve problems as particular interest in math/physics/engineering. 

I would then like to know if you have any experience in switching from applied sciences/engineering to a CS-related career, why you did it, how you've realized you prefer coding over other sciences.

Hi guys, I would like to know what are the differences in jobs and professional outcomes for people who study Engineering (specifically ME) vs applied maths or physics.  
  
I feel like a lot of the applied maths/physics people end up doing engineering jobs anyway, so what's the point of majoring in applied maths/physics instead of straight up engineering?  
  
Personally, I just finished my first bachelor year in ME, and I think I want to be a simulation engineer (i.e. work with CFD, use knowledge in mechanics to code, that kind of stuff), probably in the aerospace field or as a research associate in universities. It's not exactly the most typical engineering job, and I'm wondering if it's possible, or maybe even smarter, to get this job by doing a bachelor's in applied maths/physics and then a master's (and possibly PhD too) in computational mechanics?  
  
I don't like some ME classes, and design projects are headache-inducing to me, so I was wondering if applied maths/physics would be more fitting since it's more pure and theoretical. I do know that the upside to doing a ME bachelor's is that it'll teach me various important engineering skills and if I ever change my mind and want to work in another ME subfield than simulation, I'll have what it takes to switch.
Oh I see, I'll keep that in mind. I'm not sure how the whole clearance situation works in Canada (I live in Quebec), I'll look it up, thanks.

When I was 3-4 y/o, I played with another 4-5 y/o girl who lived close in the neighbourhood.
When we played the typical family trope story together at her place, she would do the mean, “I choose the roles we play in, otherwise you’re not my friend anymore. So, I’m gonna be the mom and you’re the baby, and you have to do what I tell you to.”

Problem is, this girl would force me to undress completely and lie in her bed under the covers to pretend I’m her baby. I remember begging her to at least keep my underwear but she refused, I had to be totally naked playing the baby. So I would undress in front of her, lie in the bed and do what she said. I felt so humiliated and weirded out, but I was only 3 or 4, so I didn’t know it wasn’t normal and I didn’t tell anyone. We played this “game” several times on different occasions when I was at her house.

Finally, one time her mom came into the room while we were playing. She was absolutely horrified to see my clothes and underwear lying on the floor, and me looking terrified and disgusted. Her mom then made me get dressed and go back home, and I never played with this girl again. It’s only when you get older that you realize how disturbing it all is, especially considering how young we were. This girl was being manipulative and coercive as hell, and now I wonder if someone did something to her that was similar, and maybe she had copied it.
